# Notification worker

The worker sends a notification through a caller-provided transport.
A transport returns true on success and false when that attempt fails.

## Delivery limit

The worker makes at most three delivery attempts for a notification.
It stops as soon as delivery succeeds and reports failure if delivery is exhausted.

For operational handling, see [the operations guide](docs/operations.md) and
[troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
The independent [download helper](docs/download-helper.md) is a separate operation.

## Local verification

No network service or third-party package is required:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```
documents.docs/download-helper.md:
# Download helper

`fetch` in `src/download.py` is independent of notification delivery.
It makes at most three attempts to obtain an artifact, stopping after success.
The caller receives false if all attempts fail. This helper does not call the
notification worker or share its retry policy.
documents.docs/operations.md:
# Operating notification delivery

This guide describes the current notification worker exposed by `deliver` in
`src/delivery.py`.

After the first failed send, the worker has two additional tries available.
Successful delivery ends processing immediately; no further copies are sent.
When the worker returns false, record the notification for operator follow-up.
Do not start a second delivery cycle automatically.
documents.docs/troubleshooting.md:
# Notification delivery troubleshooting

For the current notification worker, the third consecutive failed send exhausts
automatic delivery attempts. A false result means the notification needs
operator attention.

A true result means delivery succeeded; do not resend that notification merely
because earlier attempts failed.
documents.plans/completed/delivery-policy.md:
# Completed: initial delivery policy

Historical record of the policy before the current branch's change.
The former notification worker allowed three attempts in total: the initial
send followed by up to two further tries. Success ended the cycle early.
This records the former design, not current operating instructions.

# Notification worker

The worker sends a notification through a caller-provided transport.
A transport returns true on success and false when that attempt fails.

## Delivery limit

Delivery begins with one send. If it fails, up to three further sends are available.
It stops as soon as delivery succeeds and reports failure if delivery is exhausted.

For operational handling, see [the operations guide](docs/operations.md) and
[troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
The independent [download helper](docs/download-helper.md) is a separate operation.

## Local verification

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

documents.docs/operations.md:
# Operating notification delivery

This guide describes the current notification worker exposed by `deliver` in
`src/delivery.py`.

Use the [delivery limit](../README.md#delivery-limit) for the number of sends available.
Successful delivery ends processing immediately; no further copies are sent.
When the worker returns false, record the notification for operator follow-up.
Do not start a second delivery cycle automatically.
documents.docs/troubleshooting.md:

For the current notification worker, automatic attempts are exhausted after
the [delivery limit](../README.md#delivery-limit) is reached without success. A false result means the notification needs
operator attention.

A true result means delivery succeeded; do not resend that notification merely
because earlier attempts failed.
